name: Linux / OS kernel
short: The core that manages hardware and protected resources.
body: An OS kernel provides core resource management and privileged mechanisms such as scheduling, memory management and device interaction. Linux is a prominent implementation.
example: A process requests a file read through a system call; the kernel mediates access and coordinates the relevant system resources.
note: The Linux kernel is not a whole Linux distribution. Kernel mode is a privilege context, not a second independent meaning of kernel.

name: Lean proof kernel
short: The trusted checker of core proof terms.
body: Lean's kernel type-checks terms in its core type theory. Elaboration and tactics produce terms that this smaller trusted component checks.
example: The term fun h => h proves P→P. A tactic may find this term; the kernel checks that it has the claimed type.
note: Acceptance is relative to the declared statement and axioms. The kernel does not establish that a formal statement matches an intended informal problem; sorry introduces an assumption.

name: Jupyter / IPython kernel
short: The language process that executes notebook code.
body: A Jupyter kernel runs separately from the user interface, executes code for a language and communicates through the Jupyter messaging protocol.
example: Run x=10 in one Python cell and print(x) in another: the kernel holds the execution state. Restarting it discards that in-memory state.
note: A notebook's displayed outputs are not its live process state. This kernel is not the OS kernel or a GPU routine.

name: Microkernel
short: A small privileged OS core with services outside it.
body: Microkernels retain essential mechanisms such as isolation, scheduling and communication in the core, while many system services live in separate processes.
example: A filesystem service can execute outside the privileged core and communicate with other components using IPC.
note: The boundary varies by system. This is an OS architecture, unrelated to a BLAS microkernel.

name: Computational-geometry kernel
short: A package of geometric types, predicates and constructions.
body: A CGAL kernel supplies geometric primitives and operations: points, lines, orientation tests, intersections and more. Kernels differ in representation and exactness guarantees.
example: Exact_predicates_inexact_constructions_kernel gives exact predicate decisions while constructed coordinates may be inexact.
note: A software geometry kernel and a polygon's visibility kernel are unrelated objects, despite appearing in the same program.

name: Geometric modeling / CAD kernel
short: The engine that builds and modifies geometric models.
body: A modeling kernel supplies foundational geometry and topology operations for CAD applications, including solid modeling and operations such as Boolean combinations.
example: A CAD application uses a modeling kernel to subtract a hole from a solid or update part geometry.
note: Parasolid and Open CASCADE are examples of this software-engine sense. This is not the visible subset of a polygon.

name: Exokernel
short: A protection-focused kernel exposing low-level resources.
body: An exokernel separates resource protection from higher-level resource management. Library operating systems implement abstractions that conventional kernels often impose.
tex: \text{protection in kernel; policy in library OS}
example: An application-specific library OS can manage its own higher-level storage or memory abstractions while the exokernel enforces resource protection.
note: An exokernel is not simply a synonym for microkernel; its approach to exposing resources and placing abstractions differs.

sources.title: Exokernel: application-level resource management
sources.publisher: Engler, Kaashoek and O'Toole; Cornell course notes

name: LCF-style inference kernel
short: The small trusted code allowed to construct theorems.
body: In LCF-style systems, an abstract theorem type can be constructed only through trusted primitive inference operations. Complex proof procedures must reduce their conclusions to those operations.
example: A tactic can be large and experimental, while the operations that certify its result remain in a small inference core.
note: This architecture is related to, but not identical with, Lean's proof-term type-checking architecture.

name: Security kernel
short: The mechanisms enforcing the reference monitor.
body: A security kernel is the trusted computing-base machinery that implements the reference-monitor concept: mediating access, resisting tampering and being amenable to verification.
example: Every access to a protected object is checked against the system's access rules by the designated trusted mechanism.
note: The term may include hardware, firmware and software, and need not coincide with the whole OS kernel.

name: Simulation kernel
short: The central event scheduler and execution machinery.
body: A simulation kernel coordinates processes, events and simulated time. In SystemC, scheduling and synchronization can include delta cycles that advance computation without advancing physical simulation time.
example: A signal change schedules dependent processes; further same-time updates can run before the simulator advances to the next timed event.
note: The simulated system's time is different from wall-clock time. A GPU kernel can accelerate a simulation but is not its event scheduler.

name: Wolfram computational kernel
short: The computation engine behind the front end.
body: Wolfram's notebook front end and computational kernel are separate components. The kernel evaluates Wolfram Language expressions; the front end supplies notebook interaction.
example: A notebook can send an integration expression to the kernel and display the resulting symbolic expression.
note: A Wolfram kernel process is a computation engine. The word can also appear in mathematical kernel functions evaluated by that same process.

sources.title: The Wolfram front end and kernel
